segments.english: §7. And these are his words: "The Kabbalist, Master of the Palace of Blessing: a positive commandment on the court to inquire into and to examine the witnesses with seven inquiries, etc. There are also examinations, which are questions: what clothing he wore; the dust of the ground on which he stood, whether black, or sand, or clay; and if they contradict one another, the testimony is void. From the roots of this commandment: the included bride, the beautiful young maiden who has no eyes, the governance of this world, that there be free choice, whose eyes are like doves, a deception to the sons of man. Her eyes in the Palace of Merit: the eyes of the congregation, who judge with knowledge on the testimony of two witnesses, two crowns; and the Da'at is the secret of the eyes, as is known; and this light spreads in seven aspects." And he wrote, see there. And concerning the commandment "You shall not go about as a talebearer," he wrote: " that one should not tell his fellow that his adversary has spoken evil about him, as it is said, 'You shall not go about as a talebearer.' And the laws of the commandment: even one who speaks the truth, there is a great sin in this. And also within the scope of this prohibition: that one should not speak in disparagement of his fellow, even if true, and this is as if he denied the fundamental principle, etc." And he expanded further on the punishment of the one who tells slander and on the reward of the one who guards from it; see there.

grammar: The paragraph is two quotations. The first runs from וז"ל (3:7.2) to the author's own formula וכ' ע"ש; the words עולימתא שפירתא דלית בה עינין are Aramaic and are rendered by sense. The source is not named in the text.
מצות עשה על הב"ד לדרוש ולחקור: 'a positive commandment on the court to inquire and examine'. על with a noun reads 'incumbent upon'; the infinitives give the content of the commandment.
ואם כחשו זה לזה בטל העדות: a conditional with a perfect verb; the result clause is בטל, 'is void'. The two witnesses are the subject of the conflict (כחשו).
The second quotation begins at כתב וז"ל (3:7.93-3:7.94) and ends at וכ' (וכו'); the closing words והאריך עוד are the author's own report and take no quotation marks.
segments.note: The first quotation closes after 'seven aspects'; the author's ע"ש stands outside it. The second quotation has a Bible verse inside it, in single marks.
apparatus: Wikisource transcription. The 1931 scan is not yet collated; Wikisource additions are translated as base text (decisions, Q2).
Lev 19:16: 'לא תלך רכיל' (3:7.90-3:7.92 and 3:7.102-3:7.105). The quotation stops before בעמיך, so only the words on the page are translated.

segments.english: §8. And in the warning, "You shall not stand idly by the blood of your fellow," he wrote: "even standing by, to any degree. You shall not see your fellow's distress, that one puts him to shame, and you are silent; he stood and did not answer again. But you shall protest with all your power against him who disgraces your fellow, or speaks about him with talebearing and evil talk, You shall not be a listener and silent, but you shall say to him: 'Wicked one, troubler of Israel, why do you speak defiance against the likeness of our Maker, and against the Shekhinah, our strength, which is the yod in "among your people," and departs through this sin.' Therefore this was juxtaposed to that, 'You shall not go about as a talebearer,' and one might say: since I do not speak, I will listen and be silent, and take pleasure in what his fellow, the wicked one, speaks. This listener too is an utterly wicked person. and transgresses 'You shall not stand idly by the blood of your fellow.' He has no portion in the God of Israel when he hears a wicked one speak defiance against a righteous person, or whispers a whisper of lies about his fellow; rather, you shall immediately push him away and say to him: 'Wicked one, go away from me, I do not listen to you.' But if he hears and is silent, and all the more so if he takes pleasure, his end is to be judged in unblown fire, and he will not merit to stand in the company of the righteous, as listener, as answerer, as speaker. All of them shall perish from the world in this one, and in the world to come." Thus far his words.

וכל שכן: 'and all the more so', a kal va-chomer.
לא נופח: fire that is not fanned.
מחיצת: the enclosure, the company of the righteous.

grammar: The quotation opens with כ' (he wrote) after the verse לא תעמוד על דם רעך, and closes at עכ"ל. Within it, direct address is in single marks, and the verse לא תלך רכיל is a single-marked quotation inside the outer quotation.
ולכך נסמכה זה לזה: 'for this reason this was placed next to that'. The verse לא תלך רכיל is the second member of the pair; ותאמר begins the objection that the author answers.

וכל שכן ('all the more so') introduces the consequence. The three participles כשומע, כעונה, כמדבר ('as listener, as answerer, as speaker') are the ways of taking part, and כולם יספו ('all of them shall perish') refers back to them.
segments.note: The opening verse is in double marks because it stands outside the quotation; the verse quoted inside the quotation (3:8.90-3:8.96) is in single marks.
apparatus: Lev 19:16: 'לא תעמוד על דם רעך' (3:8.2-3:8.7 and 3:8.90-3:8.96), quoted as the author gives it.
Lev 19:16, 'בעמיך', is the source of the yod of the Shekhinah (3:8.62-3:8.63); the author's reading, not a translation of the verse's sense.
